raw_segments.text: But is this the only thing which is called odd?
Are there not other things which have their own name, and yet are called odd because,
although not the same as oddness, they are never without oddness?
That is what I mean to ask whether numbers such as the number three are not of the class
And there are many other examples.
Would you not say, for example, that three may be called by its proper name and also
be called odd, which is not the same with three?
And this may be said not only of three, but also of five, and of every alternate number
each of them without being oddness is odd, and in the same way two and four and the other
series of alternate numbers has every number even without being evenness.
